title: Earlier elimination base for MOD5 and fixed moduli

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"For every integer n>=0, MOD5_n(x)=1 exactly when the Hamming weight of its n-bit input is divisible by 5, including MOD5_0(empty)=1.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this fixed polynomial-time family in NP with empty witnesses, every full-B2 circuit computing MOD5_n has at least 2n-5 gates for every integer n>=4; consequently liminf over all integer n of C_B2(MOD5_n)/n is at least 2.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: For every fixed integer m>=3 and residue r in {0,...,m-1}, let MOD(m,r,n) be 1 exactly when the n-bit input has Hamming weight congruent to r modulo m. For every n>=m-1, its full-B2 circuit complexity is at least 2n-m. This is an unscored supporting class theorem, proved in proof.md.
